title: Polygons: Regular and Irregular, Convex and Non-Convex, and Constructing Triangles
seo_title: Grade 7 Polygons Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Draw and describe regular and irregular polygons with 5, 6, 8, or 10 sides based on measurements of sides and angles, using a ruler and protractor; draw triangles, quadrilaterals, and regular polygons (5, 6, 8, or 10 sides) with given angle measures; classify polygons according to the number of sides, whether they are regular or irregular, and whether they are convex or non-convex.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 polygons worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: names of polygons, regular and irregular, convex and non-convex, and constructing triangles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Regular: all sides equal and all angles equal.
key_sub: Convex: every interior angle is less than 180°.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A polygon is a closed figure made of straight sides. Pentagon 5, hexagon 6, heptagon 7, octagon 8, nonagon 9, decagon 10 sides.
  • A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. Otherwise it is irregular.
  • A convex polygon has every interior angle less than 180°. A non-convex (concave) polygon has a corner that points inward.
  • To draw a triangle with a ruler and protractor, the angles must add up to 180°, and the two shorter sides must add up to more than the longest side.

Examples

Example

A hexagon with all sides 4 cm, angles 120°

equal sides

equal angles

Answer: regular hexagon

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Only equal sidesA rhombus has equal sides but is not regular.
Hexagon or heptagon?Hexa- is 6, hepta- is 7.
Angles that do not add to 180°Then no triangle can be drawn.

items.q: You draw a regular decagon with a protractor. How big must each interior angle be?
items.e: The angles add up to (10 − 2) × 180° = 1,440°. Each angle: 1,440 ÷ 10 = 144°.

items.q: You draw a regular pentagon with a protractor. How big must each interior angle be?
items.e: The angles add up to (5 − 2) × 180° = 540°. Each angle: 540 ÷ 5 = 108°.

items.q: You draw a regular hexagon with a protractor. How big must each interior angle be?
items.e: The angles add up to (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. Each angle: 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.

items.q: You draw a regular octagon with a protractor. How big must each interior angle be?
items.e: The angles add up to (8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°. Each angle: 1,080 ÷ 8 = 135°.

items.q: Can sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if two sides are equal
Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 3 + 4 = 7. 7 > 5, so they make a triangle.

items.q: Can sides of 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if it is a right triangle
Only if two sides are equal
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 2 + 3 = 5. 5 < 6, so the sides cannot meet.

items.q: How many triangles have angles 60°, 70° and 50°?
c: One triangle shape, but many sizes
items.e: 60 + 70 + 50 = 180, so the angles work. But angles do not fix the size: you can draw small or large triangles with these angles.

items.q: How many triangles have angles 90°, 60° and 40°?
items.e: 90 + 60 + 40 = 190, not 180, so no triangle has these angles.

items.q: How many triangles have angles 45°, 45° and 90°?
c: One triangle shape, but many sizes
items.e: 45 + 45 + 90 = 180. Many sizes are possible.
